newsitem.title: UK: Clean tankers mainly softer in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Clean tankers mainly softer in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Clean tanker rates were softer or unchanged this week in lacklustre trade, with little sign that they are likely to perk up soon, brokers said.

Mediterranean rates, which shot up last week, have fallen on modest enquiry and plentiful tonnage. Naphtha cargoes have dipped to around W225 for 27,500 tonnes, while 28/29,000 tonne gas oil stems now pay about W200.
Brokers E.A. Gibson said that "markets, both East and West, are ticking over in neutral" and that the high Med rates seen last week seem "like a distant memory."
They said long-range owners in the Middle East experienced a frustrating week with many fixtures failing on subjects.

"Vessels open within the next couple of weeks are suffering from a lack of enquiry and will continue to offer discounted rate levels for any deals which charterers can put together," Gibson added in their weekly tanker market report.
Caribs/upcoast gas oil was flat at around W175, with rates likely to remain around this level next week, they said.
"What is needed is an increase in tonnage ballasting from the USAC to the Continent which would reduce availability in the Caribbean area and encourage an upward trend in freights," Gibson said.

The inter-U.K./Cont market was no livelier, with 20,000 tonnes flat at about W215. No gas oil trades to the east or unleaded gasoline transatlantic were heard done, brokers said. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
